mode: built-in; model and quality not controlled; exploratory, not production A/B

runs.title: Speak with confidence
runs.prompt:
Square adult editorial spot illustration in opaque colored ink and blunt dip-pen drawing. Use economical, angular, slightly uneven shapes. The drawing has lost-and-found contours: some edges have one thick mark, some a thin taper, others are left open. Faces are drawn with a handful of marks, not shaded portraits. Each eye is a small dark brush comma directly on skin-colored fill; the whites of the eyes are not drawn. Keep gaze readable through brow and head angle. Make the two faces distinct through jaw, nose, mouth placement and hair silhouette. Choose two local irregularities per person: an off-center mouth, an uneven hair edge, an unequal brow, or a fill ending short of a contour. These are deliberate drawing choices, not paper grain or random scribbles. Keep hands and object contact physically plausible. Several flat local colors against white negative space. No gradient shading, surface noise, glossy highlights, readable text, decorative filler or 3D rendering.

Scene: A middle-aged woman with short dark curly hair wearing a rust-red blouse speaks into a handheld microphone. Seen waist-up in three-quarter view, she looks toward two listeners cropped at the right edge, one in profile. Her free hand makes a relaxed explanatory gesture. A broad cobalt stage panel and a single orange stool give the scene its setting. Faces clearly visible, natural attentive expressions.
